hazards.title: Sync-Over-Async Task Deadlock (.Result in ASP.NET)
hazards.description: Calling `_oracleRepo.GetCustomerAsync(id).Result` on ASP.NET request thread causes thread-pool starvation and deadlock under load.
hazards.remedy: Always `await` async tasks or use `ConfigureAwait(false)` in library code.

hazards.title: Un-disposed OracleDataReader / CLOB Cursor Leak
hazards.description: OracleDataReader not enclosed in `await using` block. Exceeds Oracle OPEN_CURSORS limit (ORA-01000) under sustained load.
hazards.remedy: Enclose all OracleCommand and OracleDataReader instances in `await using` statements.

idiomExplainers.summary: ASP.NET Core runs request pipelines asynchronously. Blocking synchronous calls on Tasks (`.Result` / `.Wait()`) hijack thread-pool workers.
idiomExplainers.whyItMatters: Under 500 concurrent requests, thread pool exhaustion leads to 504 Gateway Timeouts.
idiomExplainers.goRule: Always use `await` end-to-end; avoid `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` in controllers.

summary: Enterprise Billing Service built on ASP.NET Core 8 and Oracle Database 19c. Analyzed ODP.NET connection lifecycles, EF Core query parameterization, and React UI bridge endpoints. Detected 1 critical Sync-over-Async Task deadlock hazard and verified 100% parameterization of Oracle SQL statements.
